prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# 10 Stocks to Beat the S&P 500 Over 2019–2023 (as of January 2, 2019)

**A caveat first:** my knowledge runs to 2026, so I know how 2019–2023 turned out and can't fully set that aside. I've limited each reason below to information public on January 2, 2019. Even so, my choice of *which* names to include is almost certainly shaped by hindsight. Treat this as an illustration, not a clean test of stock-picking.

## Market backdrop (January 2, 2019)
- The S&P 500 has just fallen nearly 20% from its September high, bottoming on December 24.
- The Fed raised rates again in December. The US–China trade war and fears of slowing growth dominate the news.
- Valuations on high-quality growth companies are the most reasonable they've been in several years.

## The 10 picks

| # | Company | Ticker | Why buy it now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Microsoft | MSFT | Azure is growing about 75% a year, and Office 365 is turning one-time license sales into subscriptions. It briefly passed Apple as the most valuable US company in November 2018. |
| 2 | Alphabet | GOOGL | It dominates search and owns YouTube, with over $100B in cash. Google Cloud and Waymo are upside the market isn't paying for. The valuation is reasonable after the selloff. |
| 3 | Amazon | AMZN | AWS is growing about 45% with high margins, and a fast-growing advertising business is raising overall profitability. The stock is down about 25% from its September high. |
| 4 | Visa | V | It's a toll-road business with network effects and roughly 50%+ net margins, and it benefits from the global shift from cash to cards. |
| 5 | UnitedHealth | UNH | The largest US health insurer, plus Optum's fast-growing data, pharmacy and care services. It adds defensive balance to a tech-heavy list. |
| 6 | Adobe | ADBE | Creative Cloud gives it a near-monopoly subscription base. The 2018 purchases of Magento and Marketo build out its Experience Cloud. |
| 7 | NVIDIA | NVDA | The stock has fallen about 50% from its October high because of a temporary glut of crypto-mining chips. Its data-center business and CUDA software ecosystem lead the market for AI and accelerated computing. |
| 8 | Costco | COST | Its membership model brings roughly 90% renewal rates and steady, recession-resistant growth. |
| 9 | Taiwan Semiconductor | TSM | It leads in 7nm chipmaking while Intel struggles with its 10nm process, and it makes chips for Apple, NVIDIA and AMD. |
| 10 | ASML | ASML | It is the only supplier of EUV lithography machines, which enter high-volume production in 2019. Every leading-edge chipmaker needs them. |

## Portfolio notes
- **Concentration:** about 70% of the list is tech or semiconductors. That sector bet is the main reason the list could beat the index, and also its main risk. UNH, COST and V add some balance.
- **Execution:** equal-weight the 10 positions, rebalance once a year, and hold through volatility. A five-year horizon only helps if you don't sell in the next drawdown.
- **The base rate:** most professional stock pickers fail to beat the S&P 500 over five years. An index fund with a smaller "satellite" position in picks like these is a reasonable alternative.

## Hindsight check
Several stocks that looked just as attractive on January 2, 2019 later disappointed:
- **Boeing** was a consensus favorite before the 737 MAX groundings.
- **Disney** was well liked ahead of the Disney+ launch.
- **Intel** and **PayPal** were also popular.

I left all of them out, and knowing the outcomes likely influenced that. This list is not a fair measure of what a forecaster in 2019 could have achieved.

This isn't personalized financial advice. I can also show how these 10 actually performed against the S&P 500 from January 2019 to January 2024.
